# Comprehensive Experimental Design: Evaluating the Recovery of Fast Timestep Dynamics by MDGEN in Subsampled Molecular Dynamics Trajectories --- ## 1. Executive Summary & Research Hypothesis Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations numerically integrate Newton’s or Langevin’s equations of motion at femtosecond timesteps ($\Delta t \approx 1\text{–}2\text{ fs}$) to capture high-frequency atomic motions (covalent bond vibrations, angle bendings, and rapid dihedral librations). In standard computational practice, storing trajectories at 1–2 fs resolution is prohibitive; trajectories are routinely decimated/subsampled by factors of $10^2$ to $10^4$ (saving every 1–10 ps). This temporal decimation induces extreme information loss, violating the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem and extinguishing high-frequency dynamic observables. **Research Question:** *Does the MDGEN generative model accurately recover the fast timestep dynamics (specifically rapid oscillations and librations in torsion angles) that are lost in subsampled molecular dynamics trajectories?* **Core Hypothesis ($H_1$):** A generative trajectory super-resolution model (MDGEN) conditioned on sparse coordinate frames $R_{t_k}$ can recover the true underlying high-frequency physical dynamics if and only if the generated ensemble preserves: 1. The characteristic high-frequency vibrational/librational peaks in the torsional Power Spectral Density (PSD) between $10^{11}$ and $10^{13}\text{ Hz}$. 2. The rapid oscillatory decay of the dihedral Autocorrelation Function (ACF) $C_{\theta}(\tau)$. 3. Physical pseudo-velocity distributions and potential energy smoothness, without suffering from harmonic over-smoothing (mean-collapse) or unphysical high-frequency hallucination. **Null Hypothesis ($H_0$):** MDGEN behaves as an effective geometric interpolator or spatial denoiser that smooths over the high-frequency librational modes (producing a low-pass filtered path) or introduces uncorrelated Gaussian white noise lacking the true physical vibrational resonances. --- ## 2. Mathematical Formulation of the Trajectory Recovery Task ### 2.1. True and Subsampled Trajectories Let a molecular system consist of $N$ atoms with Cartesian coordinates $R_t \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times 3}$ at time $t$. The ground-truth continuous-time trajectory integrated at fine timestep $\delta t = 2\text{ fs}$ over total duration $T_{tot}$ is: $$X_{\text{fine}} = \{R_0, R_{\delta t}, R_{2\delta t}, \dots, R_{T_{tot}}\}$$ A subsampled trajectory with stride $K \in \mathbb{N}$ (coarse stride $\Delta t = K \cdot \delta t$) consists of the subset of frames: $$X_{\text{coarse}} = \{R_{t_k} \mid t_k = k \cdot \Delta t, \; k = 0, 1, \dots, M\}, \quad \text{where } M = \lfloor T_{tot} / \Delta t \rfloor$$ ### 2.2. Nyquist-Shannon Information Loss & Aliasing Let $\theta(t) \in [-\pi, \pi)$ denote a designated dihedral angle calculated from four atomic coordinates $(R_{t}^{(a)}, R_{t}^{(b)}, R_{t}^{(c)}, R_{t}^{(d)})$. The local motion in a torsional potential well exhibits harmonic/quasi-harmonic libration at fundamental frequency $f_{\text{lib}} \approx 5\text{–}20\text{ THz}$ (period $T_{\text{lib}} \approx 50\text{–}200\text{ fs}$). By the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem, continuous signal reconstruction requires a sampling rate: $$f_s = \frac{1}{\Delta t} > 2 f_{\text{lib}} \implies \Delta t < \frac{T_{\text{lib}}}{2} \approx 25\text{–}100\text{ fs}$$ When $\Delta t \ge 500\text{ fs}$ or $1\text{ ps}$, the sampling rate falls deeply below the Nyquist limit ($f_s \ll 2 f_{\text{lib}}$). All high-frequency oscillatory dynamics are aliased or completely unobserved. ### 2.3. Generative Trajectory Super-Resolution Formulation MDGEN is formulated as a conditional generative model (e.g., score-based continuous diffusion or conditional flow-matching) that samples the distribution over intermediate fine trajectories conditioned on boundary/subsampled frames: $$\hat{X}_{\text{fine}}^{(s)} \sim p_\theta(X_{\text{fine}} \mid X_{\text{coarse}})$$ where $s \in \{1, \dots, S\}$ indexes independent stochastic generations. Because Langevin dynamics is intrinsically stochastic due to thermal solvent collisions, recovery cannot be judged by deterministic point-to-point coordinate trajectory matching (e.g., root mean square deviation to a specific realization). Instead, recovery must be judged by **statistical and spectral ensemble equivalence** to the ground-truth Langevin distribution. --- ## 3. Target Molecular Systems Three target systems spanning ascending degrees of conformational and solvent complexity are established: | System | Chemical Identity | Solvation Mode | Degrees of Freedom | Target Torsional Modes | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **System A: n-Butane** | $C_4H_{10}$ (Small flexible alkane) | Vacuum / Implicit | 14 atoms | Central C-C dihedral ($\chi_1$). Clean 1D 3-fold potential well with sharp, unhindered high-frequency librations ($f \approx 6.5\text{ THz}$). | | **System B: Alanine Dipeptide** | Ace-Ala-Nme | (1) Vacuum
(2) Explicit water (TIP3P, $\sim 800$ waters) | 22 solute atoms | Backbone dihedrals $\phi$ ($C-N-C_\alpha-C$) and $\psi$ ($N-C_\alpha-C-N$); sidechain methyl $\chi_1$. Tests coupled 2D Ramachandran librations and solvent friction damping. | | **System C: Chignolin** | CLN025 (10 residues: YYDPETGTWY) | Explicit water (TIP3P, $\sim 2000$ waters, neutralized $Na^+/Cl^-$) | 166 solute atoms | Backbone turns, $\beta$-hairpin hydrogen-bonded dihedrals, aromatic sidechain librations ($\chi_1, \chi_2$). Tests multi-body coupled dynamics. | --- ## 4. Ground-Truth All-Atom MD Simulation Protocols All reference simulations are performed using standard MD engines (OpenMM / GROMACS) under reproducible force field and integration parameter sets: 1. **Force Fields:** - n-Butane: OPLS-AA / GAFF2. - Alanine Dipeptide & Chignolin: CHARMM36m or AMBER ff19SB with OPC / TIP3P water. 2. **Integration Parameters:** - Integrator: Langevin leap-frog integrator. - Timestep: $\delta t = 1.0\text{ fs}$ (to eliminate integration discretization artifacts up to 500 THz). - Temperature: $T = 300\text{ K}$, friction coefficient $\gamma = 1.0\text{ ps}^{-1}$ (or $\gamma = 0.1\text{ ps}^{-1}$ for vacuum to study inertial oscillations). - Constraints: PME for long-range electrostatics (cutoff $1.0\text{ nm}$); non-bonded Lennard-Jones cutoff $1.0\text{ nm}$. Covalent bonds involving hydrogen are either unconstrained (1.0 fs step) or constrained with SHAKE/LINCS (2.0 fs step). 3. **Trajectory Generation & Storage:** - Production run per system: $100\text{ ns}$ for Alanine Dipeptide; $200\text{ ns}$ for Chignolin. - Ground-truth save stride: every $\delta t_{\text{fine}} = 2.0\text{ fs}$ ($500\text{ frames/ps}$). - Total reference frames: $5 \times 10^7$ frames per trajectory, yielding statistically converged autocorrelation functions and Fourier spectra. --- ## 5. Subsampling Regimes (Relative to Torsional Libration Frequencies) Before subsampling, the characteristic torsional oscillation frequency $f_0$ for each system is computed directly from the ground-truth reference trajectory. For alanine dipeptide in water, $\phi$ and $\psi$ librate in their potential wells with characteristic frequencies $f_0 \approx 8\text{–}15\text{ THz}$, corresponding to an oscillation period $T_0 = 1/f_0 \approx 65\text{–}125\text{ fs}$. Four systematic downsampling regimes are tested: 1. **Regime 1: Sub-Nyquist Baseline ($\Delta t = 20\text{ fs}$):** - $\Delta t < T_0 / 2$. High-frequency oscillations are preserved; tests whether the model acts as an identity/interpolation filter without corrupting observable oscillations. 2. **Regime 2: Critical Nyquist Threshold ($\Delta t = 100\text{ fs}$):** - $\Delta t \approx T_0$. The sampling rate matches the boundary where direct signal recovery becomes mathematically degenerate. 3. **Regime 3: Moderate Supra-Nyquist ($\Delta t = 500\text{ fs} = 0.5\text{ ps}$):** - $\Delta t \approx 5\text{–}8 \times T_0$. Torsional oscillations within wells are completely decimated; coarse frames observe only random instantaneous phases within the well. 4. **Regime 4: Deep Supra-Nyquist / Macro-Subsampled ($\Delta t = 5.0\text{ ps} - 10.0\text{ ps}$):** - $\Delta t \gg T_0$ and $\Delta t \approx \tau_{\text{relax}}$ (comparable to the barrier-crossing or conformational relaxation timescale). Multiple transitions and hundreds of librational cycles occur between coarse frames. --- ## 6. Baselines and Controls To unequivocally isolate MDGEN's contribution, the following baselines and controls are tested on identical subsampled endpoints: ### 6.1. Positive Controls - **$C_{\text{ref}}$ (Un-subsampled Ground Truth MD):** The exact, continuous 2 fs all-atom trajectory. - **$C_{\text{Langevin-resim}}$ (Stochastic Re-simulation):** True MD re-run initialized at $R_{t_k}$ with Maxwell-Boltzmann velocity sampling, providing the physical upper bound for stochastic path divergence under the true Hamiltonian. ### 6.2. Geometric and Mathematical Baselines - **Linear Cartesian Interpolation (LERP):** $$R_{t_k + \tau} = (1 - \alpha) R_{t_k} + \alpha R_{t_{k+1}}, \quad \alpha = \tau / \Delta t$$ *Diagnostic value:* Standard naive baseline; demonstrates steric collapse and artificial bond shortening across rotating bonds. - **Internal-Coordinate Spline Interpolation (IC-Spline):** Conversion to Z-matrix internal coordinates $(r, \theta, \phi)$, natural cubic spline interpolation along dihedrals, and reconstruction to Cartesian coordinates via NeRF (Natural Extension Reference Frame). *Diagnostic value:* Preserves bond lengths and angles perfectly while smoothly interpolating dihedrals; represents the optimal smooth, zero-vibration geometric path. ### 6.3. Physics-Based Generative Baselines - **Brownian / Langevin Bridge:** Harmonically steered/conditioned Langevin trajectory integrated at 2 fs between $R_{t_k}$ and $R_{t_{k+1}}$ using a time-dependent harmonic restraint: $$U_{\text{restraint}}(R, t) = \frac{k(t)}{2} \|R - R_{t_{k+1}}\|^2$$ *Diagnostic value:* Standard physical path-sampling method driven by the true molecular mechanics force field. ### 6.4. Machine Learning Baseline - **SE(3)-Equivariant Continuous-Time Diffusion Model:** Standard score-based diffusion model conditioned on $(R_{t_k}, R_{t_{k+1}})$ without domain-specific fast-mode physics priors. --- ## 7. Quantitative Analysis Plan & Metrics ### 7.1. Torsional Autocorrelation Function (ACF) For any continuous dihedral trajectory $\theta(t)$, compute the stationary time autocorrelation function: $$C_{\theta}(\tau) = \frac{\langle (\theta(t) - \bar{\theta})(\theta(t+\tau) - \bar{\theta}) \rangle_t}{\langle (\theta(t) - \bar{\theta})^2 \rangle_t}$$ - **True Physical Signature:** At short time lags ($\tau < 200\text{ fs}$), $C_{\theta}(\tau)$ displays underdamped or damped cosinusoidal oscillations: $$C_{\theta}(\tau) \approx \cos(\omega_0 \tau) e^{-\gamma \tau / 2}$$ - **Evaluation Metric:** $$\text{RMSE}_{\text{ACF}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{\tau_{\max}} \int_0^{\tau_{\max}} \left( C_{\theta}^{\text{MDGEN}}(\tau) - C_{\theta}^{\text{ref}}(\tau) \right)^2 d\tau}, \quad \tau_{\max} = 1.0\text{ ps}$$ ### 7.2. Power Spectral Density (PSD) and Librational Modes The frequency-domain power spectrum is computed via the Fourier transform of the windowed dihedral trajectory: $$S_{\theta}(f) = \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{1}{T} \left| \int_0^T \theta(t) e^{-i 2\pi f t} dt \right|^2$$ using Welch’s average periodogram method (Hanning window of length $2\text{ ps}$, $50\%$ overlap). - **Evaluation Sub-metrics:** 1. **Peak Resonance Frequency Error:** $$\Delta f_{\text{peak}} = |f_{\text{peak}}^{\text{MDGEN}} - f_{\text{peak}}^{\text{ref}}|$$ 2. **High-Frequency Spectral Band Power Ratio ($5\text{–}25\text{ THz}$):** $$\mathcal{R}_{\text{band}} = \frac{\int_{5\text{ THz}}^{25\text{ THz}} S_{\theta}^{\text{MDGEN}}(f) df}{\int_{5\text{ THz}}^{25\text{ THz}} S_{\theta}^{\text{ref}}(f) df}$$ - $\mathcal{R}_{\text{band}} \approx 1.0 \implies$ Accurate vibrational power recovery. - $\mathcal{R}_{\text{band}} \ll 1.0 \implies$ Artificial over-smoothing (loss of fast dynamics). - $\mathcal{R}_{\text{band}} \gg 1.0 \implies$ High-frequency noise hallucination. 3. **Spectral Cosine Similarity:** $$\mathcal{S}_{\text{cos}} = \frac{\int_0^{f_{\max}} S_{\theta}^{\text{MDGEN}}(f) S_{\theta}^{\text{ref}}(f) df}{\sqrt{\int S_{\theta}^{\text{MDGEN}}(f)^2 df} \sqrt{\int S_{\theta}^{\text{ref}}(f)^2 df}}$$ ### 7.3. Finite-Difference Pseudo-Velocities & Vibrational Density of States (VDOS) Because MDGEN outputs coordinates $R_t$, define the numerical central-difference pseudo-velocity vector: $$V_i(t) = \frac{R_i(t + \delta t) - R_i(t - \delta t)}{2\delta t}$$ The mass-weighted Velocity Autocorrelation Function (VACF) is: $$C_v(\tau) = \sum_{i=1}^N m_i \langle V_i(t) \cdot V_i(t+\tau) \rangle_t$$ The overall Vibrational Density of States (VDOS) is: $$g(f) = \int_0^\infty C_v(\tau) \cos(2\pi f \tau) d\tau$$ - **Metric:** Wasserstein-1 distance $\mathcal{W}_1(g^{\text{MDGEN}}, g^{\text{ref}})$ across the vibrational spectrum ($0\text{–}50\text{ THz}$). ### 7.4. Physical and Geometric Integrity Metrics 1. **Bond Length and Angle RMSD:** $$\text{RMSD}_{\text{bond}} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{N_{\text{bonds}} T} \sum_{t} \sum_{(i,j)} (\|R_i(t) - R_j(t)\| - d_{ij}^0)^2}$$ 2. **Steric Overlap Frequency:** Percentage of atom pairs with distance $r_{ij} < 0.7 \times (\sigma_i + \sigma_j)$ (van der Waals overlap threshold). 3. **Potential Energy Roughness / Distribution:** Evaluate the potential energy $U(R_t)$ of MDGEN frames using the host force field; compare $p(U^{\text{MDGEN}})$ to $p(U^{\text{ref}})$ via Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. --- ## 8. Feasibility, Confounding Factors, and Mitigation Strategies 1. **Path-Level Non-Determinism (Stochasticity) vs. Frequency Recovery:** - *Confounder:* For Langevin dynamics at 300 K, two trajectories starting from identical coordinates diverge exponentially within a few hundred femtoseconds (Lyapunov time $\approx 100\text{ fs}$). Evaluating MDGEN via trajectory-wise coordinate RMSD against the reference will erroneously penalize physically correct stochastic paths. - *Mitigation:* The primary evaluation must be strictly **distributional and spectral**. Individual realizations are evaluated via PSD, ACF decay rates, and ensemble-averaged vibrational densities over $S \ge 50$ stochastic model generations. 2. **Boundary Discontinuities & Conditioning Seams:** - *Confounder:* Models conditioning on $R_{t_k}$ and $R_{t_{k+1}}$ may exhibit artificial kinetic "kicks" or velocity discontinuities at boundary knots. - *Mitigation:* Explicitly compute the acceleration distribution $\ddot{R}(t)$ across the stitched boundaries $t = t_k \pm \delta t$ to test for boundary seams. 3. **Solvent Coupling and Damping:** - *Confounder:* In explicit solvent, high-frequency dihedrals undergo frequent solvent collisions, damping oscillations much faster than in vacuo. - *Mitigation:* Compare alanine dipeptide in both vacuum and explicit solvent. If MDGEN only captures unhindered harmonic oscillations (vacuum) but fails in explicit solvent (or vice-versa), the role of stochastic solvent friction is cleanly decoupled. --- ## 9. Definitive Evaluation & Decision Criteria To provide a decisive, evidence-based answer to the research question: | Outcome Classification | Quantitative Criteria | Scientific Interpretation | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Full Accurate Recovery** | 1. Spectral band power ratio $0.85 \le \mathcal{R}_{\text{band}} \le 1.15$ in Regime 3 ($\Delta t = 0.5\text{–}1.0\text{ ps}$).
2. Peak frequency error $\Delta f_{\text{peak}} < 0.5\text{ THz}$.
3. $\text{RMSE}_{\text{ACF}} < 0.10$.
4. $\text{RMSD}_{\text{bond}} < 0.03\text{ \AA}$ (no unphysical distortions). | **YES.** MDGEN accurately learns the underlying physical Hamiltonian and recreates the true high-frequency librational modes lost in downsampling. | | **Partial / Over-Smoothed Recovery** | 1. $\mathcal{R}_{\text{band}} < 0.40$ (under-estimation of high-frequency power).
2. ACF decays monotonically without high-frequency cosinusoidal oscillations ($\text{RMSE}_{\text{ACF}} > 0.30$).
3. Geometric bonds are preserved. | **NO (Over-smoothing).** MDGEN behaves as a spatial/geometric low-pass filter (similar to spline interpolation), producing realistic static conformers but failing to recover the fast dynamic oscillations. | | **Artifactual / Noisy Recovery** | 1. High-frequency power present but diffuse with no resonant peak ($\mathcal{S}_{\text{cos}} < 0.50$).
2. Steric clashes $> 1\%$ or high unphysical potential energy spikes. | **NO (Hallucination).** MDGEN injects high-frequency geometric jitter or unstructured noise rather than physical librational dynamics. | --- ## 10. Conclusion and Execution Blueprint This experimental design establishes an end-to-end framework: - By systematically probing from sub-Nyquist ($\Delta t = 20\text{ fs}$) to deep supra-Nyquist ($\Delta t = 10\text{ ps}$) intervals across Butane, Alanine Dipeptide, and Chignolin, it isolates the exact temporal boundary where dynamic information breaks down. - By utilizing spectral power densities, torsional autocorrelation decays, and finite-difference VDOS alongside geometric baselines (IC-Spline) and physical baselines (Langevin bridge), it eliminates confounding factors and delivers an unambiguous answer to whether MDGEN captures true sub-picosecond molecular mechanics.
